name: Halogens
kicker: Group 17 of the periodic table · The “salt-forming” elements
briefing: The halogens are the six elements of group 17: fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine, and tennessine. Their name means “salt-former,” because they react eagerly with metals to make salts, like the sodium chloride on your dinner table. Fluorine is the most reactive element of all, chlorine keeps swimming pools clean, and bromine is one of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature.
answerHtml: Halogens (accept group 17 or group VIIA elements; prompt on group 7)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Henri Moissan [“mwah-SAHN”] won the 1906 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for isolating the lightest of these elements, which he finally managed in 1886 by electrolysis. The heaviest of these elements, tennessine, was first made in 2010 and named for a U.S. state.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements, including fluorine and chlorine, whose atoms have seven valence electrons.

tossups.p: The second-lightest of these elements has the highest electron affinity of any element, even higher than the lightest one. The lightest of these elements forms a surprisingly weak bond with itself, weaker than the bond between two atoms of the second-lightest.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of reactive elements, whose name means “salt-former,” that includes fluorine and chlorine.

tossups.p: With hydrogen, the members of this group form acids, and only the one made with the lightest member, which can etch glass, is a weak acid. Two different members of this group can bond together in compounds like chlorine trifluoride.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements that gain one electron to form ions with a −1 charge, such as chloride and bromide.

tossups.p: Astatine, the rarest naturally occurring member of this group, was first made at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1940, and its name comes from the Greek word for “unstable.” Its lighter neighbor in this group, iodine, is named for the Greek word for “violet.”
tossups.r: These diatomic elements sit just left of the noble gases. For 10 points, name this group that includes fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine.

tossups.p: Bernard Courtois [“koor-TWAH”] discovered one of these elements in the ashes of seaweed in 1811. Antoine Balard [“bah-LAR”] announced the discovery of another one in 1826, and its name comes from the Greek word for “stench.”
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements, including iodine and bromine, which form salts when they react with metals.

tossups.p: Silver compounds of these elements are so sensitive to light that they made old-fashioned photographic film work, and a silver compound of one of them is sprayed into clouds to help make rain or snow.
tossups.r: Iodine is added to table salt to keep the thyroid gland healthy. For 10 points, name this group of elements whose name means “salt-former.”

tossups.p: Thomas Midgley Jr. helped develop refrigerants called CFCs, which contain two of these elements and were later phased out by the 1987 Montreal Protocol to protect the ozone layer. These elements become less reactive going down their group.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements, including fluorine and chlorine, that form salts with metals.

tossups.p: Some very bright light bulbs contain a small amount of iodine or bromine, which helps their glowing tungsten filaments last longer. Chlorine, another member of this group, is used to disinfect swimming pools and drinking water.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements whose atoms have seven valence electrons and form ions with a −1 charge.

tossups.p: The heaviest member of this group, element 117, was first made in 2010 by a team of Russian and American scientists and named for the state of Tennessee. Another member of this group, astatine, is radioactive and extremely rare.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements that also includes fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine.

tossups.p: Two different members of this group can bond to each other, forming compounds such as chlorine trifluoride and iodine heptafluoride. Moving down this group, the atoms get larger and the elements become less reactive.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements, each of which needs just one more electron to fill its outer shell.

tossups.p: When chlorine water is added to a solution of potassium bromide, the mixture turns orange-brown because chlorine pushes out the less reactive member of this group, an example of a displacement reaction.
tossups.r: Fluorine is the most reactive member of this group. For 10 points, name this group of elements whose name means “salt-former.”

tossups.p: At room temperature, the lightest two members of this group are gases, the third is a reddish-brown liquid, and the fourth is a gray-black solid that turns directly into a violet vapor when heated.
tossups.r: These elements react with sodium to form salts such as table salt. For 10 points, name this group of elements just left of the noble gases.

tossups.p: Grignard [“green-YAR”] reagents are made by reacting magnesium metal with a carbon compound containing one of these elements, such as bromine. Fluorine, the most reactive member of this group, is also the most electronegative element.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of elements, including chlorine and iodine, whose atoms have seven valence electrons.

tossups.p: Humphry Davy proved that one of these elements was an element, not a compound, and named it after the Greek word for “pale green.” Carl Wilhelm Scheele [“SHAY-luh”] had first produced that element in 1774.
tossups.r: These elements form salts with metals like sodium. For 10 points, name this group of elements that includes chlorine, fluorine, and iodine.

tossups.p: Roy Plunkett accidentally discovered the nonstick plastic Teflon in 1938, and it is made of carbon and the lightest of these elements. Iodine, another member of this group, is added to table salt to keep the thyroid gland healthy.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this group of reactive elements with seven valence electrons each.

clues.t: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine, and tennessine
The column just left of the noble gases on the periodic table
Each atom has seven valence electrons and gains one electron to form an ion with a −1 charge
Their name comes from Greek words meaning “salt-former”
React with metals such as sodium to make salts like sodium chloride, table salt
They exist as diatomic molecules such as F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, and I₂
At room temperature, fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a liquid, and iodine is a solid
Bromine is one of only two elements that are liquid at room temperature; the other is mercury
Iodine is a gray-black solid that turns into a violet vapor when heated; its name comes from the Greek for “violet”
Reactivity decreases going down the group; fluorine is the most reactive element of all
Their −1 ions are fluoride, chloride, bromide, and iodide
A more reactive one displaces a less reactive one from a salt: chlorine turns potassium bromide solution orange-brown
Chlorine disinfects pools and drinking water, fluoride fights tooth decay, and iodine is added to “iodized” salt
Fluorine is the most electronegative element
Their acids with hydrogen are strong, except hydrofluoric acid, which is weak but can etch glass
Two different members bond to each other in compounds like chlorine trifluoride and iodine heptafluoride
Chlorine has the highest electron affinity of any element, higher even than fluorine’s
The bond in a fluorine molecule is surprisingly weaker than the bond in a chlorine molecule
Henri Moissan isolated fluorine in 1886 by electrolysis and won the 1906 Nobel Prize in Chemistry
Carl Wilhelm Scheele first made chlorine in 1774; Humphry Davy proved it was an element and named it for its pale green color
Bernard Courtois found iodine in seaweed ash (1811); Antoine Balard announced bromine (1826), whose name comes from the Greek for “stench”
Astatine, first made at Berkeley in 1940, is radioactive and very rare; its name means “unstable”
Tennessine, element 117, was first made in 2010 by Russian and American scientists and named for Tennessee
Light-sensitive silver compounds of these elements made photographic film work; silver iodide is used to seed clouds
Thomas Midgley Jr. helped develop CFC refrigerants; the 1987 Montreal Protocol phased them out to protect the ozone layer
Some bright light bulbs use iodine or bromine to help their tungsten filaments last longer
Grignard reagents are made from magnesium and a carbon compound containing chlorine, bromine, or iodine
Roy Plunkett discovered Teflon, made of carbon and fluorine, in 1938

trap.title: The family, not one member
trap.body: Tossups on this group are packed with single-element clues, like fluorine’s reactivity, chlorine in pools, or bromine as a liquid, which tempts players to blurt one element’s name. But the question wants the whole family. The noble gases, one column to the right, are the other trap: they almost never react, while these elements are among the most reactive on the periodic table.
trap.fix: Listen for “these elements” or “this group,” and answer with the family name. Seven valence electrons, −1 ions, “salt-former,” and diatomic molecules mean this group; full outer shells, glowing neon signs, and almost no reactions mean the noble gases.
trap.line: Real answer line: Halogens (accept group 17 or group VIIA elements; prompt on group 7)
